reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the order and refund data myself so I can catch any problem that would justify a hold.
The orders list is in, so next I'll pull the refunds ledger to confirm W2's claimed refunds match what's recorded before any net balances are computed.
The refunds ledger matches W2's report: orders 201 and 203 with the same amounts. Nothing looks wrong, so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 54385 matches my own check: orders 200 and 203 total 73072, less the 18687 refund on order 203. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 40147 matches my check: orders 201 and 204 total 44020, less the 3873 refund on order 201. Cobalt has no refunds in the ledger, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 33079 matches my check: orders 202 and 205 total 33079, with no refunds. All three balances agree with my own calculations and the refunds ledger matches W2's report, so nothing justifies a hold. I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 40147, which matches my own calculation from orders 201 and 204 less the refund on 201.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's balance of 33079 matches my own calculation from orders 202 and 205 with no refunds. I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my independent calculation from the orders and refunds ledger, so the batch is complete and I'm finishing with the report.
